note.p: Irish radical, collaborator with William Thompson on An Appeal from one Half of the Human Race to the Other. LIved in Paris in the 1820s, returning to London where she was a meeting place for French Socialists and radicals. The dates fit with her times in London from the DNB article. The Wheeler at Lady Caroline Lamb's does not have a feminine title, but Godwin often dropped it especially for independent-minded women. It could also have been Mrs Wheeler's daughter Rosina, as Edward Bulwer Lytton was present and would propose to her the next month, see Rosina Bulwer Lytton DNB 1802-1882. The last entry above confirms the identity as she was with her uncle Sir John Doyle DNB 1756-1834
